YOUR PRESENTATION COMPANION

What should we explain?

Our purpose: Plan useful CPU work within an assumed resource budget and reduce unnecessary calculations.

  1. Choose tasks: whole jobs use 0/1 Knapsack; partial jobs use Fractional Knapsack.
  2. Reduce calculations: Matrix Chain Multiplication finds the cheapest grouping.
  3. Manage priority: Binomial and Fibonacci heaps process the same jobs.
  4. Previous results: a B-Tree retrieves saved runs.

Quick demo

Budget 5 → choose whole tasks (benefit 9). Enable partial tasks → choose again (benefit 9.8). Run the matrix example (27,000 → 4,500). Set budget 15 with whole tasks to admit all three; in step 3 make Data processing urgent. Finally retrieve a saved result.

What is optimization?

Finding the best valid answer: maximize benefit within the budget, or minimize the matrix multiplication count.

Does it cool the CPU?

No. Resource costs are assumed and calculations are counted. We do not measure temperature or execute the sample application jobs.

Where is the code?

algorithms.js contains the actual algorithms. app.js connects the interface, algorithms and browser history. index.html and style.css form the interface. No server or database service is required.

Complexity

0/1: O(nW) time and space (pseudo-polynomial). Fractional: O(n log n) time, O(n) space. Matrix chain: O(m³) time, O(m²) space. Binomial heap operations: O(log n) worst case. Fibonacci: insert O(1), decrease-key O(1) amortized, extract-min O(log n) amortized. Both heaps use O(n) space. Fixed-degree B-Tree search/insert: O(log r), storage O(r), excluding record contents.

n = tasks; W = budget; m = matrices; r = records. General 0/1 optimization is NP-hard; its decision form is NP-complete. Do not label the entire application NP-hard.

Browser storage rewrites all saved records; that cost is separate from B-Tree lookup. Saved runs are limited to the latest 200. Heap timings vary; neither heap is always faster.
